question.text: For futures or options contracts NOT officially listed on a market (OTC), the realisation value shall be:

answer.text: Determined by the investment manager using a defined method
Taken as the last exchange settlement of a similar contract

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the chapter: 'The realisation value of futures or options contracts not officially listed on a market or traded on an unregulated market should be the net realisable value as determined by a method determined by the Investment Manager.' The Trap: Assuming a value of zero is absurd; using the exchange settlement of a similar listed contract distorts the OTC instrument's economics; investee-company reporting is irrelevant to derivative valuation. Note: For unlisted or unregulated-market derivatives, the workbook places the obligation to set and apply the valuation method on the Investment Manager.
